text:
Andrew Peeke has become an unlikely scorer in Utah. The defenseman, in his first season with the Mammoth after stops in Columbus and Boston, has 4 goals in 26 games, including goals in back-to-back games on Nov. 21 against Anaheim and Nov. 23 against Winnipeg.

Enjoy it while it lasts. Those 4 goals came on 1.2 expected (the quality of his shots), and he's shooting 15% after 6% last season. That finishing rate rarely holds, and our talent range for his scoring sits far below his current pace. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, with his team creating little when he was out there, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows only 24% of his exits keeping possession.

There is something in the clutch column, though: his goals have added 0.66 wins by our count against 0.18 expected, which means they came at moments that mattered. The Mammoth have lost a pile of overtime games lately. Peeke is a defense-first piece on 18 minutes a night, and the goals are a happy accident, not a new identity.
headline: Peeke is finishing like a forward
